user: A weekly GitHub repo tracker now lives at the repo root — deploy it next to your Railway Postgres to start building stars/forks/issues time series every Sunday.
what: Added the GitHub Repo Tracker app: a weekly Railway Cron service that upserts GitHub repos and metric snapshots (stars, forks, open issues, watchers, size) into the project's Postgres over internal networking, plus wiki pages documenting the app and the Railway cron/private-networking pattern.
why: The project needs durable numerical tracking of GitHub repos over time; this gives it a cheap, idempotent pipeline (one runtime dep, minutes of compute per week) with zero manual schema management.
next: See README.md at the repo root for the 5-step Railway deploy, or sql/queries.sql for the time-series queries you can run once data lands.

Deployed as Railway cron writing to project Postgres over internal networking. Verified live GitHub dry-runs and Railway docs facts; recorded Entity + Concept pages.

user: Wiki now explains exactly which GitHub endpoints the tracker uses (and why /user/repos isn't one of them), so nobody reintroduces the wrong repo source later
what: Added two learnings to the knowledge wiki: the difference between GitHub's /user/repos, /users/{owner}/repos, and /search/repositories endpoints (what the tracker uses today, the 1,000-result search cap, and what switching to private repos would entail), and a workflow gotcha that failed edit batches apply nothing rather than partially. Also repaired two broken wiki links on the GitHub Repo Tracker entity page.
why: The endpoint distinction came up as a direct user question and the answer (public-owner + search only; private repos need a repo-scoped token and break the contributor-count stat) isn't obvious from the code alone — documenting it prevents a future session from wiring /user/repos in without understanding the consequences.
next: See docs/wiki/learnings/github-repo-list-endpoint-semantics-user-repos-vs-users-owne.md before touching any repo-listing API call
summary: Recorded two learnings: (1) GitHub repo-list endpoint semantics — /user/repos (token-accessible, may include private) vs /users/{owner}/repos (public, used by GITHUB_OWNERS) vs /search/repositories (1,000/query cap, used by GITHUB_SEARCH_QUERIES), plus private-repo knock-on effects for the contributors-based collaborator stat and the undecided GITHUB_SOURCE_SELF option; (2) edit batches are atomic — a failed edit means nothing in that batch landed. Also fixed two broken relative links in the GitHub Repo Tracker entity page (scope decision + Railway networking pattern).

user: The tracker can now watch every public repo on your own GitHub account: set GITHUB_SOURCE_SELF=1 plus your token, and each Sunday's run stores stars, forks, watchers, collaborators and open issues for all of them.
what: Added a self source (GITHUB_SOURCE_SELF=1) that lists all public repos of the configured GitHub account via /user/repos and stores weekly stat snapshots for each — on top of the existing owner-listing and search sources.
why: The user wants their own account's public repos tracked weekly; /user/repos is the authenticated endpoint that enumerates them without listing owners manually.
next: On Railway, set GITHUB_SOURCE_SELF=1 + GITHUB_TOKEN (and DATABASE_URL if not yet set), then trigger a first run via a temporary schedule; query the time series with sql/queries.sql.
summary: Added GITHUB_SOURCE_SELF=1 source to github-repo-tracker: GET /user/repos?visibility=public with pagination, requires GITHUB_TOKEN (startup-validated). Entity page updated with the third source type. Pushed as f72a9b9.

user: The repo tracker now has a clear, achievable weekly target: every public GitHub repo with more than 50 stars
what: Recorded a decision setting the tracker's coverage threshold: all public repos with >50 stars (via search API), resolving the open question from the earlier "harvest all public repos" decision.
why: GitHub caps search at 1,000 results/query, so the >50-star bar is what makes full coverage actually implementable — future sessions building the source need this criterion and the range-splitting technique.
next: Implement the sharded stars:>50 discovery source, then update the GitHub Repo Tracker entity page
summary: Recorded decisions/tracker-coverage-threshold-all-public-repos-with-50-stars.md — the user's ">50 stars" direction operationalizes the pending "harvest ALL public repos" decision into an implementable, completely-enumerable target via recursive star-range splitting; no code changes landed this turn.

user: The wiki now has hard feasibility numbers for tracking 142k+ repos weekly — so the upcoming sliced-search build starts from measured costs, not guesses
what: Added two learnings: sliced-search sweep cost/size measurements (weekly slices, ~65–75 min/sweep, FETCH_DETAILS must be off or multi-token at 142k-repo scale) and the GitHub search quirk that watchers_count just mirrors stargazers_count.
why: These numbers answer the open size/FETCH_DETAILS questions left by the >50-stars coverage decision and prevent two silent data bugs (truncated single-page fetches, watchers=stars duplication).
next: See docs/wiki/learnings/sliced-search-sweep-numbers-142k-repo-corpus-fits-weekly-cro.md before implementing the sliced discovery source
summary: Recorded two learnings from the large-corpus feasibility analysis: (1) measured sweep numbers — 142,457 repos match created:>=2022-01-01 stars:>=100, weekly date slices required (monthly exceeds the 1k search cap), ~1,900 search calls ≈ 65–75 min at 30 req/min, and detail fetching at that scale needs ~57 h/token/week so big sweeps require FETCH_DETAILS=0 or multi-token; also rolling-window and page-1-only gotchas from the user's example script. (2) GitHub search payloads report watchers_count == stargazers_count; true watchers only via the per-repo detail endpoint. No decision recorded — the sliced-search + FETCH_DETAILS=0 proposal awaits user confirmation.
